0.text: The client’s journey starts when a new service is needed: they enter the store and look for a specific service. They then decide whether to take a turn ticket; if not, the visit ends there. If they do take a ticket, they indicate where it was taken: if via the app, they choose the service, wait, and then look for the product and its specific criteria before checking how many tickets are ahead; if taken physically, they proceed directly to waiting. In both cases, after waiting they ask for a specific request, which is sent to the request assistant, who is active during the registration period. Upon receiving the client’s request, the assistant registers it and checks whether enough requests have accumulated to respond to demand; if not, registration continues with the next request, but once enough requests exist the assistant sends the order request document and closes the registration phase. That document reaches the shop assistants, who prepare the order and then deliver it, notifying the client to collect the order. The client collects the order and decides whether to make a new request; if yes, they return to looking for a specific service, and if no, their process ends. Independently, the shop assistants can also start preparation upon receiving an order description, and they conclude with preparation finished after delivery.

1.text: When a new service is initiated, the client enters the store, looks for a specific service, and, if one is found, takes a ticket for his or her turn. Depending on where the ticket is taken, either via the app or physically at the location, the client proceeds differently: via the app, the client first chooses the service, waits for the indicated time, then looks for the product with specific criteria, checks how many tickets are ahead, waits for his or her turn, and asks for a specific request; if taken physically, the client waits for his or her turn and then asks for a specific request. If no suitable service is found, the client ends the visit. The specific request is communicated to the request assistant, who, at the scheduled register time, registers the request and evaluates whether there are enough requests to respond to customer demand; if not, registration repeats until there are enough. Once there are enough, the request assistant sends the order request document and concludes their part of the process. The order request document is transmitted to the shop assistants’ team, which may also begin when an order description is received; they prepare the order and then deliver it, notifying the client. The client collects the order and decides whether a new request is needed: if yes, the client returns to looking for a specific service and the cycle continues; if no, the client’s process ends. The shop assistants finish their work after delivery once preparation has been completed.

2.text: When a new service is needed, the client enters the store and looks for a specific service; if no ticket is required, the interaction ends immediately. If a ticket is required, the client takes a ticket and, depending on where it was taken, either chooses the service in the app or waits physically for their turn. In the app case, after choosing the service, a waiting period ensues; during this time the client looks for the product and specific criteria, checks how many tickets are ahead, and returns to waiting. In both the physical and app paths, when it is their turn the client asks for a specific request, which is sent to the request assistant for registration. On the assistant side, at the register time, the request is registered; if there are not yet enough requests to respond to customer demand, registration continues until there are; once there are enough, the order request document is sent and registering is over. That document is passed to the shop assistants’ team, which prepares the order and then delivers it; upon delivery, a notification is sent to the client, who collects the order. The client then decides whether there is a new request: if yes, they go back to look for a specific service; if no, their process is ended. The shop assistants close their part when preparation is finished.

0.text: The process starts with the HR clerk retrieving the requirement profile and then the job posting. Based on this, the clerk prepares a co‑signature note and forwards it for review. The section manager reviews the note and decides whether there are comments. If there are comments, the process returns to the clerk to prepare and forward a revised co‑signature note again. If there are no comments from the section manager, the note is passed to the department head for review. The department head then decides whether there are comments. If the department head has comments, the process returns to the clerk to prepare and forward a revised co‑signature note, after which it is reviewed again by the section manager and, if needed, once more by the department head. If the department head has no comments, the process ends.

1.text: The process starts when the clerk begins by retrieving the requirement profile and then retrieves the job posting. The clerk prepares a co‑signature note and forwards it. The section manager reviews the forwarded note and decides whether there are comments. If there are comments, the flow returns to the clerk to recreate the co‑signature note and continue as before. If there are no comments at this stage, the note is checked by the department head, who also decides whether there are comments. If the department head has comments, the process loops back to the clerk to recreate the co‑signature note and proceed again. If the department head has no comments, the process ends.

2.text: The process starts when the clerk retrieves the requirement profile and then retrieves the corresponding job posting. From there, the flow moves to a central decision point that leads the clerk to draft a co-signature note, which the clerk then forwards for review. The section manager reviews the note and decides whether there are comments: if yes, the flow returns to the central point and the clerk prepares and forwards a revised co-signature note again; if no, the note proceeds to the department head. The department head reviews the note and decides whether there are comments: if yes, the flow likewise returns to the same central point so the clerk can revise and resend the note; if no, the process ends. This loop continues until both the section manager and the department head indicate there are no comments, at which point the process concludes.

0.text: The process starts when the travel details are fixed. A check-list for preparations is prepared and then the necessary papers are checked and completed. A decision is made whether a visa is required: if Yes, an application for a visa is submitted and a communication is sent to the embassy; if No, this is skipped. In either case, the next step is to clear unfinished business, after which it is decided whether there are pets to take care of. If Yes, care for the pets is arranged before proceeding; if No, this is omitted. Next, the post is unsubscribed or a neighbour is asked to fetch it, after which the necessary vaccination is obtained and insurance coverage is checked, applying for further coverage if necessary, which triggers a communication to the insurance company. The preparations then branch into three activities that are carried out in parallel: gathering travel documents and addresses, preparing a first-aid kit, and buying or lending guidebooks and city maps. Once all three are completed, copies of ID cards and travel documents are made, and the process concludes with the travel preparations completed.

At this point, if the patient is considered suspicious, the pharmacist contacts the GP for advice; the GP replies, and the pharmacist provides advice/recommendations, after which the decisions are confirmed and the case ends unfilled. An appointment is then set once the customer confirms it, after which a customer conversation takes place. Based on that, a specification sheet is written and the resulting information is sent to the customer; the process then waits for and receives the customer’s feedback. With that input, project and capacity planning is performed, standard open-source products are checked, use cases are defined, and costs are calculated. A decision is made whether it is a new development or based on existing products: for existing products, the knowledge management systems are adjusted accordingly; for new products, the product is developed. The flow then continues to product acceptance, in which the customer participates, followed by obtaining customer feedback. Follow-up projects are identified, and the order is completed. Communications with the customer during the process include the appointment confirmation to set the meeting, the transmission of information after the specification sheet, the reception of feedback to proceed with planning, participation in the acceptance, and the provision of further feedback during the feedback collection.

0.text: When the existing corporate designs are deemed outdated, the marketing department begins by conducting brainstorming. The outcome is passed to the designer, who designs a new element. This design is then assessed, leading to a review of the designs and, based on that, the designer creates templates. The templates are sent back to marketing to review. If marketing finds the templates satisfactory, the team conducts communication with management and then reassesses whether the templates are satisfactory in light of that communication; if confirmed, the new corporate designs are adopted and the process ends. If marketing’s initial review is not satisfactory, or if the post‑communication confirmation is not satisfactory, the work is routed back to the designer for rework, which returns to the assessment of the design, followed by reviewing the designs again and recreating the templates. This loop continues until the templates are confirmed satisfactory after communication with management, after which the new designs are put into use.

1.text: When Existing Corporate Designs are Outdated, the Marketing department conducts brainstorming and then hands over to the Designer to design new element. The work proceeds to review designs, after which the Designer creates templates. The Marketing department then reviews templates and decides “Template satisfactory?”. If Yes, the Marketing department conducts communication with management, after which it again decides “Template satisfactory?”. If the answer is Yes at this second decision, the process concludes with Use new corporate designs. If the answer is No at this second decision, the flow returns to the Designer to continue with review designs and repeat the cycle of creating templates and reviewing templates. Likewise, if the first “Template satisfactory?” decision yields No, the process also routes back to the Designer, merges, and revisits review designs, then proceeds again through create templates, review templates, and the same two-step satisfaction and communication cycle until the template is satisfactory after management communication, at which point it ends with Use new corporate designs.

If the templates are satisfactory at this point, marketing conducts communication with management and then checks again whether the templates are satisfactory. If management agrees, the process completes with the new corporate designs being used. If either marketing’s review or management’s check finds the templates unsatisfactory, the flow is sent back to the designer for rework: the process returns to the design stream, continues with reviewing the designs again, recreating the templates, and repeating the marketing review (and, if passed there, the management communication and final check) until the templates are satisfactory and the new designs are adopted.

3.text: When the existing corporate designs are outdated, the marketing department begins by conducting brainstorming, after which the designer creates a new element. After the communication with management, marketing performs a second satisfaction check: if the outcome is yes, the organization adopts and uses the new corporate designs; if the outcome is no, the process again returns to the designer’s loop for further iteration (assessment, review of designs, and template creation) before coming back to marketing for another review and decision. This cycle repeats until the satisfactory outcome is reached and the new designs are put into use.

If the candidate is rejected at this stage, a rejection is created and sent to the applicant, and the process ends with the applicant rejected after preselection. Otherwise, the application documents are examined in detail, and it is decided whether the application concerns a key position: if yes, a telephone interview is conducted and then the appointment for a personal interview is communicated via email; if no, the appointment for a personal interview is communicated via email directly. After this communication, either the appointment is adjusted and the communication repeated, or the appointment and applicant documents are forwarded to the department. The personal interview is then conducted, after which a decision is taken on whether to proceed with an assessment center. If the assessment center is required, preparation and scheduling run in parallel before converging to conduct the assessment center; afterwards, a vote on applicants is held. If the assessment center is not required, the vote on applicants is held directly after the personal interview. Based on the vote, either an acceptance is written and sent to the applicant, ending with the applicant accepted, or a rejection is drafted and sent to the applicant, ending with the applicant rejected after the assessment center.

0.text: The process starts in risk management, where two background checks are launched in parallel: a BKR check and a Jane Doe check. Once both checks have been completed, a combined assessment is performed through a credibility check, after which senior risk management confirms the outcome. If the assessment is rejected, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends. If the assessment is accepted, customer contact calls the client to complement the information; if the information has not yet been picked up, the team waits one hour and calls again, repeating this cycle until the information is picked up. Once it is picked up, a loan offer is created and then sent to the client. The team then waits for the client’s reaction: either the accepted offer is received, or, after one hour without a response, the client is reminded and the waiting cycle continues until acceptance arrives. Upon receiving the accepted offer, a welcome letter is sent, the loan application is activated, its activation is validated, the initial payment is executed, and the documents are returned to the client, after which the process ends.

0.text: The customer’s journey begins, they place an order, and this order is communicated to the kitchen where the waiter forwards it to the sous chef. The waiter’s work starts with sending the order to the sous chef, after which the sous chef organizes and manages the order of cooking. The chef then cooks the dish and, once finished, hands it over to the sous chef. The sous chef checks the food and, when satisfied, calls the waiter to pick it up. The waiter then sends the food to the customer, completing the kitchen’s work. As the food is sent, a notification reaches the customer, who then enjoys the meal and concludes their part of the process.

1.text: Two processes run in parallel and exchange messages. On the customer side, the flow begins with Start, after which the customer proceeds to Order food. This order is sent to the kitchen as a message that arrives at Send order to Sous Chef. In the kitchen, the waiter’s flow starts with Start and immediately moves to Send order to Sous Chef; from there, the sous chef continues with Manage the Order of Cooking, which triggers the chef to begin Cooking. Once Cooking is finished, the chef performs Send to sous chef, after which the sous chef carries out Check the food and then Call waiter to grab food. The waiter then performs Send food to customer and the kitchen flow ends with End. The dispatch of the dish is communicated to the customer as a message that triggers Enjoy food, after which the customer process concludes with End.

2.text: The customer’s journey starts when they begin and place an order, after which they proceed to enjoy the food and then finish. In parallel, the kitchen begins and immediately has the waiter pass the order along to the sous chef. The sous chef then organizes the cooking sequence and hands it to the chef, who cooks the dish and hands it back to the sous chef. The sous chef checks the food and then calls the waiter to pick it up. The waiter sends the food to the customer and then the kitchen side finishes. Two communications occur between the two parties: the customer’s order is sent to the waiter’s activity that forwards the order to the sous chef, and later the waiter’s delivery of the food triggers the customer’s step of enjoying the meal.

If teachers are involved, they activate learning progress in the selected objects and then continue to the point where the status is prepared. If students are involved, they click on “Learning Progress” for each object, after which it is decided whether the status is set manually by the user or determined automatically by the instructor. In the manual case, the user sets the status; in the automatic case, the instructor’s determination is applied. Both the teachers’ and students’ paths then converge to show the status via a color marking. From there, one of four outcomes is shown: a red cross indicates failure (for courses, tests, and exercises), green indicates fully processed, yellow indicates in progress, and gray indicates not yet started. Regardless of which color appears, the paths merge and the process ends.

0.text: At SoKnow, the process starts when the HR department begins organizing employee interviews and sends the employee appointment suggestions. From there, three strands proceed in parallel: HR conducts the employee interview, HR conducts regular inquiries, and the employee confirms the appointment. After confirming, the employee participates in the employee meeting and then completes the assigned training, after which the process concludes on their side with training completed. On the HR side, once the interview has been conducted, HR assigns the training. The HR branch with the assigned training and the branch with the regular inquiries proceed until both are finished, at which point the HR portion concludes with the employee interview being recorded as conducted.

0.text: The process starts when the user comes to the library, after which the user logs in. The user’s request is then determined: if the request is to extend, the media is extended; if instead it is to borrow, a medium is selected. For a borrow request, the selected medium is searched in the database; if it is not available, a “Medium not available” notification is sent to the external party, and the process waits for a response. The external party can reject the reservation, in which case the rental process is aborted, or confirm the reservation, after which the reservation process is carried out and the process ends with the medium being reserved. If the database search shows the medium is available, the user is identified and the process ends with the medium being lent. For an extension request, after extending the media a decision is made: if the outcome is yes, the process ends with “Media extended”; if the outcome is no, it ends with “Medium will be returned.”

1.text: The process starts when the user comes to the library and logs in. Next, a decision is made about the user’s request: if the user wants to extend, the media is extended and then it is checked whether the extension is permitted; if it is, the process ends with the media extended, and if not, it ends with the medium to be returned. If the user wants to borrow, the user selects a medium and it is searched in the database; if it is available, the user is identified and the process ends with the medium to be lent. If it is not available, the user is informed that the medium is not available, after which the process waits for a response: the external library user may send a rejection of the reservation, which ends the process with the rental aborted, or may send a confirmation of the reservation, after which the reservation process is performed and the process ends with the medium to be reserved.

2.text: The process starts when a user comes to the library and logs in. The user’s request is then clarified: if the intent is to extend, the media is extended; if the extension is confirmed, the process ends with media extended, otherwise it ends with the medium to be returned. If the intent is to borrow, a medium is selected and searched for in the database. If it is available, the user is identified and the process ends with the medium to be lent. If it is not available, a notification that the medium is not available is sent to the external library user, after which the process waits for a response: upon receiving a confirmation, the reservation process is carried out and the process ends with the medium to be reserved; upon receiving a rejection, the process ends with the rental process aborted.

3.text: The process starts when a user comes to the library and logs in. The user then states the request: either to extend an existing loan or to borrow an item. If the request is to extend, the system attempts to extend the medium; if the extension is granted, the process ends with the media extended, otherwise it ends with the medium being returned. If the request is to borrow, the user selects a medium and the system searches the database. If the medium is available, the user is identified and the process ends with the medium being lent. If the medium is not available, a notification is sent to the external library user, after which the process waits for a response: if the external user confirms the reservation, the reservation process is carried out and the process ends with the medium being reserved; if the external user rejects the reservation, the process ends with the rental being aborted.

0.text: The process starts with an application for IMIS and proceeds by going to the fh‑swf website and defining the search criteria. Next, three selections are made in parallel: Informatics and Digitalization is chosen as the subject area, the Master study course is selected, and Campus Soest is chosen. Once all three choices are completed, the applicant clicks “Find a Study Course,” then “Learn more” on the IMIS banner, and then “See how to apply here.” The application procedure is reviewed, after which the path depends on whether the applicant is from the EU. If not, the applicant follows the Non‑EU/International route, applies via Uni‑Assist, sends the required documents to Uni‑Assist, and then waits for a decision within 10–12 weeks. If the applicant is from the EU, two tracks are carried out in parallel: one identifies the applicant as an FH‑SWF student/graduate who applies via the FH‑SWF online portal and then contacts the IMIS office, and the other proceeds as an EU applicant who applies via the FH‑SWF online portal, sends the required documents, and then contacts the IMIS office. After both EU tracks are completed, the applicant waits for a decision within 4–6 weeks. In either case, the process continues to a decision point and ends with the receipt of either an admission or a rejection letter.

1.text: The process starts with Application for IMIS and continues by going to the fh-swf website, then defining the search criteria. Based on that, three selections are made in parallel: the subject area is set to Informatics and Digitalization, the study level is set to Master, and the campus is set to Soest. Once all three have been completed, the next steps are to click Find a Study Course, click the Learn more link on the IMIS banner, and then click See how to apply here. The procedure is then reviewed, after which it is determined whether the applicant is from the EU. If not, the path proceeds with Non-EU/ International Applicant, followed by applying via Uni-Assist and sending the required documents to Uni-Assist; after that a decision is awaited within 10–12 weeks before proceeding to the outcome. If the applicant is from the EU, two steps are carried out in parallel: indicating FH-SWF Student/Graduate and confirming EU Applicant. From the FH-SWF Student/Graduate branch, the application is submitted via the FH-SWF Online Portal and the IMIS Office is contacted. From the EU Applicant branch, the application is submitted via the FH-SWF Online Portal, the required documents are sent, and then the IMIS Office is contacted. After both EU branches have reached the IMIS Office, the process waits for a decision within 4–6 weeks before proceeding to the outcome. In both cases, the process concludes with the Receipt of Admission/ Rejection Letter.

0.text: The process starts when a sales enquiry request is received from the customer, which creates the sales enquiry. The enquiry is then routed based on its origin: if it is for an outbound customer, an enquiry is created; if it is for an inbound customer, a contact is created. From there, the case proceeds to assess whether the price is acceptable and there is interest. At this point, an approval request is sent to the customer and the process waits for the customer’s approval to be received. Once the response arrives, the outcome branches: if the price is not approved, the enquiry status is updated and the process ends with the client not approving; if the price is approved, a quote is created, a requirements analysis is performed, the enquiry status is updated, a job is created, and the process ends with the job created.

1.text: The process starts when a sales enquiry request from the customer arrives, triggering the creation of a new sales enquiry. It is then determined whether the customer is outbound or inbound: for an outbound customer, an enquiry is created; for an inbound customer, a contact is created. In both cases the path continues to qualify that the price is acceptable and there is interest. At this point, an approval is sent to the customer and the process waits until the customer’s approval is received. Once received, a decision is made: if the price is not approved, the enquiry status is updated and the process ends with the client not approving; if the price is approved, a quote is created, followed by a requirements analysis, then the enquiry status is updated, and finally a job is created, after which the process ends with the job created.

2.text: The process starts when a sales enquiry request arrives from the customer, upon which a sales enquiry is created. Depending on the origin of the lead, if it is an outbound customer the team creates an enquiry, while for an inbound customer a contact is created; both paths then converge to qualify price acceptance and interest. At this point a request for approval is sent to the customer, and the team waits until the customer’s approval is received. If the price is not approved, the enquiry status is updated and the process ends with the client not approving. If the price is approved, a quote is created, a qualified requirements analysis is performed, the enquiry status is updated, and a job is created, after which the process ends with the job created.

3.text: The process starts when Accentis receives a Sales enquiry request from the Customer, which triggers Sales enquiry created. The enquiry is then classified: for an Outbound customer, Create enquiry is performed; for an Inbound customer, Create contact is performed. In both cases, the work proceeds to Qualified Price OK and Interest, from which Accentis sends Customer approval sent to the Customer and then waits for Customer approval received. Once the approval arrives, a decision is made: If price is not approved, Update enquiry status is carried out and the process ends with Client does not approve. If price is approved, Create Quote is performed, followed by Qualified Requirements analysis, then Update Enquiry Status, and finally Create Job, after which the process ends with Job created.

4.text: The process at Accentis starts when a sales enquiry request from the customer is received, thereby creating the sales enquiry. 0.text: When a supplier inquiry arrives, the warehouse clarifies the question with the specialist department and then reaches a waiting point where one of three things can occur: a further inquiry from the supplier, an actual delivery of parts, or the lapse of five working days without delivery. If the delivery arrives, the quantity and quality are checked; if the result is acceptable, the goods are stored and, upon receipt of a customer order, the warehouse prepares and packages the goods and completes shipping/goods issue. If the check fails, a replacement delivery is requested and the supplier is notified, after which the process returns to the same waiting point. If five working days pass without delivery, the warehouse contacts the supplier to determine whether immediate shipping is possible; if it is, the process returns to the waiting point, otherwise it concludes with delivery issues. Independently, once a bill of materials has been created, goods are ordered and the process also joins that same waiting point. The communications are as follows: the supplier sends inquiries and delivery notifications, the warehouse sends the replacement delivery request to the supplier, and the sales unit sends the customer order that triggers preparation, packaging, and goods issue.

1.text: The process is driven by external communications. When a supplier inquiry is received, warehousing clarifies the question with the specialist department and then proceeds to a wait state in which it either receives a delivery of parts from the supplier, receives another supplier inquiry, or reaches a timeout after five working days without delivery. If five days pass without delivery, warehousing contacts the supplier to check whether immediate shipping is possible: if it is not, the process ends with delivery issues; if it is, the process returns to the wait state. If a delivery of parts arrives, warehousing checks the quantity and quality; if the check fails, a replacement delivery is requested and this request is sent to the supplier before returning to the wait state; if the check succeeds, the goods are stored and warehousing then waits for an order from Sales. Upon receipt of the order, goods are prepared and packaged and then shipped/issued. In addition, when needed, a bill of materials may be created and goods ordered, after which the flow also returns to the same wait state. Communications that occur are: receipt of supplier inquiries and delivery notifications from the supplier, sending of a replacement-delivery request to the supplier when the check fails, and receipt of the order message from Sales to trigger preparation and shipping.

2.text: The flow can start in several ways. If an inquiry arrives from the supplier, the warehouse clarifies the question with the specialist department and then moves to wait for the next event: either another inquiry from the supplier, an actual delivery of parts, or the lapse of five working days without delivery. If five days pass without delivery, the warehouse contacts the supplier and checks whether immediate shipping is possible; if yes, the process returns to the same waiting point for the next inquiry or the delivery, and if not, it ends with delivery issues. If a delivery of parts arrives from the supplier, the warehouse checks quantity and quality and evaluates the result: if this check fails, a replacement delivery is requested and communicated to the supplier, after which the flow returns to the earlier decision point that leads back to waiting for the next inquiry or the delivery; if the check is successful, the goods are stored. Once the goods are in storage, the process waits for an order from Sales; upon receipt of that order, the goods are prepared and packaged and then shipped (goods issue). In addition, a separate path may create a bill of materials and order goods; once goods have been ordered, the flow reaches the same decision point used above, from which it proceeds to wait again for either an inquiry, a delivery, or the five-day timeout that triggers contacting the supplier.

3.text: The process reacts to external triggers from two sides. When a supplier inquiry arrives, the warehouse clarifies the question with the specialist department and then waits for one of three things to happen: another inquiry from the supplier, an announcement of delivered parts, or the passage of five working days without any delivery. If a delivery notice from the supplier arrives, the warehouse checks the quantity and quality; if the check fails, a replacement delivery is requested and this request is sent to the supplier, after which the process returns to the earlier waiting point. If the check succeeds, the goods are stored and the process waits for an order message from Sales; upon receipt of that order, the goods are prepared and packaged and then shipped (goods issue). If instead five working days pass without a delivery, the warehouse contacts the supplier and determines whether immediate shipping is possible; if so, it returns to the waiting point for the next supplier message or delivery, and if not, the process ends with an escalation due to delivery issues. In addition, there is an internal sequence where a bill of materials is created and the goods are ordered, after which control returns to the same decision point. The communications that occur are: the supplier sends inquiries and delivery announcements to the warehouse; the warehouse sends a replacement delivery request to the supplier when quality or quantity fails; and Sales sends the customer order to the warehouse to trigger preparation, packaging, and shipment after storage.

4.text: The flow revolves around an ongoing cycle in warehousing that waits for external developments. It begins by awaiting one of three situations: a supplier inquiry arrives, parts are delivered, or five working days pass without a delivery. If a supplier inquiry is received from the supplier, the warehouse clarifies the question with the specialist department and then returns to wait again. If parts are delivered by the supplier, the warehouse checks their quantity and quality; if this check succeeds, the goods are stored and the process then waits for an order from Sales. Once the order message is received from Sales, the goods are prepared and packaged, followed by shipping/goods issue. If the quantity or quality check fails, the warehouse requests a replacement delivery and sends this request to the supplier, then resumes waiting. If instead no delivery occurs within five working days, the warehouse contacts the supplier and assesses whether immediate shipping is possible; if it is, the process returns to wait for the next incoming development, but if not, it ends with delivery issues. Independently, the warehouse may create a bill of materials and then order goods; once goods are ordered, the flow returns into the same waiting cycle for either a supplier inquiry, a delivery, or the five-day timeout.

If an inquiry from the supplier arrives, it is received and the question is clarified with the specialist department; in either case, the flow reaches a decision point where Warehousing waits for one of three events: a further supplier inquiry, the delivery of parts, or the passage of five working days without delivery. If another inquiry comes in from the supplier, it is received and again clarified with the specialist department, returning to the same waiting point. If the parts are delivered, the quantity and quality are checked; if this check succeeds, the goods are stored and Warehousing then waits for an order message from Sales, upon which the goods are prepared and packaged and then shipped (goods issue). If five working days pass without delivery, the supplier is contacted and it is determined whether immediate shipping is possible: if yes, the flow returns to the waiting point; if not, the process ends due to delivery issues. 0.text: The process starts at ACME AG when a need arises. The stock is checked first. If the required work equipment is in stock, it is retrieved from the storeroom and the process ends with the work equipment removed from the storeroom. If it is not in stock, the requirements are specified and quantified, then an order is placed. From there, either the receipt of the work equipment is awaited or, after five days without receipt, the order is placed by e-mail to the supplier. After the e-mail order is sent, receipt of the work equipment is awaited again. The supplier sends a notification of receipt of the work equipment back to ACME AG, which is accepted regardless of whether it arrives in response to the initial order or the e-mail order. Once the receipt is registered, the process concludes with the work equipment procured.

0.text: The process starts when the need to secure personnel development is recognized. First, employee data is analyzed. Based on this, three activities proceed in parallel: personnel capacity is checked, capacity requirements are determined, and training opportunities are identified. Once all three are completed, an employee interview is conducted. The outcomes of the interview trigger three concurrent follow-ups: training is allocated, any training request is considered, and improvement suggestions are considered. When these parallel actions are finished, the results are brought together and discussed with the department head. Training or continuing education is then organized, after which the competency profile is updated. The process ends with personnel development needs secured.

0.text: At Hochschule Mainz, the process starts with “Solve problems,” after which a ticket is received. It is then decided whether participation of the customer is necessary. If yes, Support contacts the customer, conducts a detailed interview on the problem, and connects to the customer’s client system. Together with the customer, the problem is worked on, after which further information is requested. Based on that, it is checked whether to continue working on the solution or proceed: if more work is needed, the process returns to solving the problem with the customer; if not, the problem is marked as solved. If customer participation is not necessary, Support proceeds to solve the problem without involving the customer and then marks the problem as solved. In both cases, Support creates notes for documentation, sends a confirmation that the ticket is completed, and the process ends with “Problems solved.”

1.text: The process at Hochschule Mainz starts when a problem needs to be solved, and a ticket is received by Support. It is then decided whether the participation of the customer is necessary. If yes, Support contacts the customer, conducts a detailed interview on the problem, and connects to the customer’s client, after which the joint “Support; Customer” role attempts to solve the problem. This is followed by asking for further information, and a decision is made whether the problem is resolved: if not, the work returns to solving the problem; if it is, the path continues. If customer participation is not necessary, Support proceeds to solve the problem without involving the customer. In both cases, once the problem is solved, Support records notes for documentation and then issues a confirmation that the ticket has been completed, after which the process ends with the problems solved.

tasks.name: Conduct detailed interview on the problem

2.text: The process begins with a request to solve problems, after which the ticket is received by Support and a decision is made on whether the customer needs to participate. If participation is required, Support contacts the customer, conducts a detailed interview on the problem, and connects to the customer’s client environment. Together with the customer, the problem is tackled; if more details are needed, further information is requested and an assessment follows on whether additional work is required. If more work is needed, the effort returns to solving the problem and may iterate through requesting information and reassessing until no further work is necessary. Once the problem is considered resolved, notes are created for documentation, a confirmation that the ticket is completed is sent, and the case is closed. If customer participation is not necessary, Support solves the problem without involving the customer, then proceeds directly to mark the problem as solved, create documentation notes, send the completion confirmation, and finish with the problems solved.

If more input is needed, further information is requested; based on that, either the work continues with solving the problem (repeating the cycle of solving and requesting more information as necessary) or it is recognized as solved. If customer participation is not required, Support solves the problem without involving the customer. In both cases, once the problem is solved, notes are created for documentation, a confirmation that the ticket is completed is sent, and the process ends with the problems solved.

The applicant then completes the missing information, after which the loan provider admits the document and the process ends with the provisioning being finished.

0.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant, upon which an acknowledgment of receipt is sent back to the applicant. The application is then checked, and its status is decided: if the outcome is “invite,” an invitation to a job interview is sent to the applicant, after which an employment contract is prepared and the interview is conducted. Based on the interview result, if the applicant is suitable (“Yes”), the employment contract is sent to the applicant, the process waits until the signed employment contract is received from the applicant, and it ends with the signed contract available. If the applicant is not suitable (“No”), a rejection is sent to the applicant and the case is closed as the applicant rejected. Alternatively, if the initial status decision is “reject,” a rejection is sent to the applicant and the case is likewise closed as the applicant rejected.

tasks.name: Sign and send signed employment contract

1.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant. The HR department immediately sends an acknowledgment of receipt to the applicant and then checks the applicant. Based on the resulting application status, either a rejection is sent to the applicant and the process is concluded with the applicant rejected, or the applicant is invited to a job interview. If invited, the HR department prepares the employment contract and conducts the interview. After the interview, a decision is made on whether the applicant is suitable. If not suitable, a rejection is sent to the applicant and the process again ends with the applicant rejected. If suitable, the employment contract is sent to the applicant. The process waits until the signed employment contract is received back from the applicant, after which it ends with the signed employment contract available. Throughout the process, the following communications take place with the applicant: the initial application triggers the process; the acknowledgment of receipt is sent after the application is received; an invitation is sent if the applicant is to be interviewed; a rejection may be sent either after the initial check or after the interview if the applicant is not suitable; the employment contract is sent if the applicant is suitable; and finally the signed contract is returned by the applicant to complete the process.

2.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant, upon which an acknowledgment of receipt is sent back to them. The application is then checked to determine the application status: if the result is “invite,” an invitation to a job interview is sent to the applicant, after which the employment contract is prepared and the interview is conducted; if the result is “reject,” a rejection is sent to the applicant by the HR manager. Following the interview, the question “Applicant Suitable?” is decided: if “Yes,” the employment contract is sent to the applicant, and the process waits until the signed employment contract is received from the applicant; once it is received, the process ends with the signed employment contract available. If “No,” a rejection is sent to the applicant, after which the process ends with the applicant rejected. In both rejection paths (either after the initial application check or after the interview), the process concludes with the applicant rejected.

tasks.name: Send rejection to applicant (after initial check)

3.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant by the HR department, which immediately sends an acknowledgment of receipt back to the applicant and then checks the applicant. Based on the application status, either a rejection is sent by the HR manager to the applicant, after which the process moves to a merge and ends with the applicant being rejected, or the HR department invites the applicant to a job interview and then prepares the employment contract before conducting the interview. After the interview, a decision is made on whether the applicant is suitable: if not, the HR department sends a rejection to the applicant, which merges into the same rejection end; if suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the applicant. The process then waits to receive the signed employment contract from the applicant; once it is received, it concludes with the signed employment contract being available. Throughout the process, the following communications take place with the applicant: the initial application sent to start the process, the acknowledgment of receipt from HR, the interview invitation from HR, any rejection notices (either from the HR manager before the interview or from the HR department after the interview), the employment contract sent by HR, and the signed employment contract returned by the applicant.

4.text: The process starts when an application is received from the Applicant, which triggers the HR department to send an acknowledgment of receipt back to the Applicant. The case then moves to the HR manager, who checks the applicant and decides on the application status. If the decision is to reject, the HR manager sends a rejection to the Applicant, after which the case concludes with the applicant rejected. If the decision is to invite, the HR department invites the Applicant to a job interview and then prepares the employment contract before conducting the interview. After the interview, the applicant’s suitability is assessed. If the applicant is suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the Applicant and waits until the signed employment contract is received from the Applicant; once it arrives, the process ends with the signed employment contract available. If the applicant is not suitable, the HR department sends a rejection to the Applicant, after which the case concludes with the applicant rejected.

After the interview, the applicant’s suitability is decided: if suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the applicant and waits to receive the signed document, after which the process ends with the signed employment contract available; if not suitable, the HR department sends a rejection to the applicant and the case then closes as rejected. Based on the application status, either a rejection is issued or the applicant is invited to an interview. If a rejection is decided at this stage, the HR manager sends a rejection message to the applicant and the process proceeds to the outcome that the applicant is rejected. If an invitation is decided, the HR department sends an interview invitation to the applicant, then prepares the employment contract, and conducts the interview. After the interview, if the applicant is suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the applicant and waits until the signed employment contract is received from the applicant; once it is received, the process ends with the signed employment contract available. If the applicant is not suitable after the interview, the HR department sends a rejection to the applicant, which leads to the same outcome that the applicant is rejected. If the decision is to invite, an interview invitation is sent to the applicant, the employment contract is prepared in advance, and the interview is conducted. Based on the interview result, if the applicant is not suitable, a rejection is sent by the HR department and the process again joins at the same consolidation point and ends with the applicant being rejected. If the applicant is suitable, the employment contract is sent to the applicant and the process waits until the signed employment contract is received back from the applicant; upon receipt, the process finishes with the signed employment contract available. Communications with the applicant occur when the application is submitted to start the process, when the acknowledgment is sent, when the interview invitation is sent, when a rejection is sent (either by the HR manager or the HR department, depending on the decision path), when the employment contract is sent, and when the signed contract is returned.

If suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the Applicant and waits to receive the signed contract back from the Applicant; once the signed employment contract is received, the process ends with the signed employment contract available. Communications exchanged during the process include: the Applicant’s initial application to start the process, the acknowledgment of receipt, the interview invitation, either of the possible rejections, the employment contract sent to the Applicant, and finally the Applicant’s return of the signed employment contract.

0.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant. Human Resources immediately sends a receipt confirmation back to the applicant, then verifies the applicant and determines the application status. If the application is accepted, an invitation to a job interview is sent to the applicant, after which the employment agreement is prepared and the job interview is carried out. Based on the interview, a suitability decision is taken: if the applicant is suitable, an employment contract is sent to the applicant, and upon receipt of the signed employment contract from the applicant, the process ends with the signed employment contract being present. If the applicant is not suitable after the interview, a rejection is sent to the applicant and the process concludes with the applicant being rejected. If, instead, the application status is rejected earlier, a rejection notification is sent to the applicant and the process proceeds to the same conclusion that the applicant is rejected. All external communications are exchanged with the applicant: the initial application triggers the start, the receipt confirmation is returned to the applicant, the interview invitation is sent to the applicant, the rejection (and its notification) are sent to the applicant when applicable, the employment contract is sent to the applicant when suitable, and the signed contract is then received back from the applicant before concluding.

If the application is rejected at this point, a rejection notification is issued to the applicant and the process proceeds to the outcome that the applicant is rejected. If the application is accepted, the Human Resources Department invites the applicant to a job interview, prepares the employment agreement, and then conducts the interview. Based on the interview result, a decision is made on whether the applicant is suitable. If suitable, an employment contract is sent to the applicant; once the signed contract is received from the applicant, the process ends with the signed employment contract being present. If not suitable, a rejection is sent to the applicant, after which the flow joins with the earlier rejection path and concludes with the outcome that the applicant is rejected.

0.text: The process starts when sample products are requested by the Warehouse Supervisor. The request leads to the supplier, who iterates on providing samples: the supplier first adjusts product specifications as needed and then provides sample products; the Warehouse Supervisor evaluates whether the samples meet the requirement. If they do not, the supplier adjusts the specifications and provides new samples again; if they do, the Warehouse Supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order. This triggers internal coordination to the supplier’s side to check stock availability. If stock is not available, the supplier restocks inventory; whether stock was already available or has just been replenished, the flow proceeds to send the product. The Warehouse Supervisor receives the product and checks it, then decides whether the physical delivery matches the order. If they do not match, the Warehouse Supervisor requests the missing products, which routes back to the supplier to check stock and continue until the remaining items are sent and received. Once the delivery matches the order, the Warehouse Supervisor sends a payment authorization to the Department, which processes the payment and then notifies the supplier, after which the process ends with the supplier being notified.

tasks.name: Select product and send purchase order

1.text: The process starts when sample products are requested by the warehouse supervisor. The request triggers the supplier to provide sample products; these are evaluated, and if they do not meet the requirements, the supplier adjusts the product specifications and provides new samples, repeating this cycle until the samples meet the requirements. Once acceptable samples are confirmed, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order. This leads into a check of stock availability at the supplier: if stock is not available, the supplier restocks inventory before proceeding; if stock is available, the process moves directly forward. In either case, the supplier then sends the product, which is received by the warehouse supervisor and checked. If the delivered items and the order do not match, missing products are requested and the process loops back to the step preceding the stock check, after which availability is reassessed and the remaining items are sent as needed. If the delivery matches the order, payment authorization is sent, the department processes the payment, and the supplier is notified, at which point the process ends.

8.text: The process starts when sample products are requested. The supplier is then engaged to provide sample products, after which the samples are evaluated: if they meet the requirement, a product is selected; if they do not, the product specifications are adjusted and the supplier provides new samples, repeating this cycle until the samples meet the requirement. Once a product is selected, a purchase order is sent, which triggers checking stock availability at the supplier. If stock is not available, inventory is restocked before proceeding; if stock is available, the process continues directly. In either case, the next step is to send the product, which is then received and checked. If the physical products do not match the order, missing products are requested and the process returns to the stock check at the supplier to fulfill the remaining items, after which delivery, receipt, and checking are repeated. When the order and the physical products match, payment authorization is sent, payment is processed, and the supplier is notified, at which point the process ends with the supplier notified.

9.text: The process starts when sample products are requested by the warehouse supervisor. A request is issued to the supplier to provide sample products, upon which the samples are evaluated: if they do not meet the requirement, the supplier adjusts the product specifications and the request for samples is repeated; if they meet the requirement, the warehouse supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order. The order is then routed to check stock availability at the supplier. If stock is not available, inventory is restocked and then the flow continues; if stock is available, it proceeds directly to prepare for shipment. In both cases, the supplier sends the product, after which the warehouse supervisor receives it and checks the products. The received items are compared against the order: if they match, the warehouse supervisor sends a payment authorization, the department processes the payment, and the department notifies the supplier, after which the process ends with the supplier notified. If the received items do not match the order, the warehouse supervisor requests the missing products, which returns the flow to the point before checking stock so that availability is checked again (with restocking if needed) and another shipment is sent, after which receipt and checking repeat until the order and physical product match.

0.text: The process starts with the risk manager initiating two assessments in parallel: a BKR check and a Jane Doe check. Once both assessments have yielded acceptable results, a credibility check is performed. If this evaluation is deemed acceptable, it is confirmed by the senior risk manager, after which a decision is taken on the credibility assessment: if it is rejected at this point, a rejection letter is sent by the administrator and the process ends; otherwise, customer relations calls the client to complement any missing information. Based on the outcome of that call, if the client has provided the requested information, a loan offer is created; if not, the team waits for one hour and then reminds the client, returning to the decision until the information is picked up. After the loan offer is created, it is checked and then sent to the client. Customer relations then waits either for the client’s acceptance of the offer or for one hour to elapse; if an hour passes without a response, the client is reminded and the waiting resumes. When an accepted offer is received, a welcome letter is sent and finance activates the loan application, validates the activation, executes the initial payment, and returns the documents to the client, after which the process ends.

0.text: The process starts when the customer seeks to resolve a problem through customer service. The customer first recognizes the problem, then contacts customer service and describes the problem. The consultation team takes over to identify the problem, find a suitable solution, and describe that solution back to the customer. The customer then attempts to fix the problem based on the described solution and assesses whether the solution is helpful. If it is considered helpful, the customer proceeds to implement the solution, after which the case concludes with the problem fixed. If it is not considered helpful, the customer requests a new solution, the consultation team suggests further solutions, and the process then concludes with the problem fixed.

0.text: The process starts with booking an appointment, where the patient requests an appointment. The patient then submits a request describing the problem, which prompts the receptionist to verify available dates. If there are no dates available within 90 days, the appointment is rejected and the process ends. If dates are available, the receptionist makes an appointment and sends the time and date to the patient. The patient reviews the appointment details and decides whether to confirm them. If the patient does not confirm, the flow returns to requesting an appointment. If the patient confirms, the patient sends personal data, after which an email with the patient’s data is handled and the appointment is registered, ending with the appointment successfully completed.

1.text: The process starts when booking an appointment begins. The patient first requires an appointment and, with that request, a message is received that describes the problem. Based on this, the receptionist verifies the available dates and decides whether any slots exist within 90 days. If no dates are available in that period, a rejection message is sent and the process ends for that request. If dates are available, the receptionist makes the appointment and sends the specific time and date. The patient then checks the received appointment details and decides whether to confirm. If the patient does not confirm, the process returns to requiring an appointment again. If the patient confirms, the patient sends personal data, which triggers an email containing the patient’s data to be received and used to register the appointment. Once registered, the process finishes with the appointment done.

0.text: The process starts when a customer wants a credit and fills out the credit application, after which the application is sent to a mediation agency. The agency forwards the request to both banks in parallel: it triggers the loan request at Bank B and the credit inquiry at Bank A. At Bank A, the request leads to a check of the credit amount; if the amount is greater than 20 times the monthly income, a rejection is issued to the agency; otherwise, a 20% annual interest is estimated and a credit report is sent back to the agency. At Bank B, the request leads to a check of the credit amount and then to an assessment of whether the applicant’s income lies between €2,000 and €100,000; if not, a rejection is sent to the agency; if it does, the bank performs interest rate determination and then sends a credit report to the agency. Based on what returns from the banks, the mediation agency either sends a credit proposal or a rejection to the customer. After sending the application, the customer waits for whichever arrives first: receipt of a rejection or receipt of a credit proposal; upon receiving either, the case is evaluated and the credit process is completed.

0.text: When parts are required in the department, the situation is first assessed to determine availability. If parts are in stock, the department retrieves them from storage and the process ends with the parts retrieved from storage. If parts are not in stock, the department specifies and quantifies the requirements and then completes a purchase order, which is passed to Central Purchasing for checking. Based on whether the vendor is known, Central Purchasing either proceeds directly or first creates a new vendor; in both cases the process converges and an order template is created from the purchase order. The order is then sent to the approver for approval. Once approved, Central Purchasing handles the receipt of goods and, if everything proceeds without incident, the process concludes with the parts procured. However, if delivery problems are escalated during the receipt of goods, the order status is adjusted and the process ends with cancellation due to delivery problems.

0.text: The process starts when a late payment is received and the finance department informs management. It is then checked whether the customer has already been reminded. If so, the finance department inquires with the customer and sends an inquiry email (“Nachfrage”) to the customer company. Depending on whether a response is received, either an online banking check is performed and the case proceeds to posting the payment, after which the process ends with the payment processed, or, if no response arrives, the case is handed over to legal: the legal department is notified to engage a lawyer, a request (“Anfrage”) is sent to the external lawyer, and the legal team runs the target reminder process; this branch ends with the payment processed in the legal track. If the customer had not been reminded, the legal department creates a reminder and sends it (“Mahnung”) to the customer. After sending the reminder, it is determined whether payment has been made. If not, another reminder cycle is initiated; if repeated attempts fail (after a third unsuccessful reminder), the finance department is notified, the case is escalated to legal, a request is sent to the external lawyer, and the legal team runs the target reminder process to its conclusion, where the payment is recorded as processed. If payment has been made after a reminder, two things happen in parallel: the reminder effort is completed, and the case continues through the financial posting path by aligning with the payment-check track; the payment is then posted and the process ends with the payment processed.

Based on this review, the work proceeds to a phase where two activities are carried out in parallel: the development department designs new content while also updating existing content. Once both are finished, the results are synchronized and two further activities run in parallel: the development department permanently updates the content, and the marketing department evaluates the content. If the evaluation is positive, the marketing department informs management and the process concludes with the website currently needing no improvements. If the evaluation is not positive, the process returns to the point after the review so that the design and update activities are repeated. Independently of the evaluation branch, when the permanent update is completed the process can also conclude with the website being up to date.

If the answer is yes, a follow-up step without a label is performed and the process enters a diagnostic phase: as applicable, the following issues are handled in parallel—no power, no image, hard drive not recognized, and boot loop—each through its own unlabeled step. Once all relevant issues have been addressed and the work converges, another unlabeled step is carried out and installation feasibility is reassessed. If at this point installation is not possible, the flow returns to the earlier unlabeled step to iterate the diagnostics; if it is possible, a final unlabeled step is performed and the process ends. 0.text: A hotel guest sends an order to the hotel, which the room service manager receives and responds to by creating and forwarding an order ticket. From there, three work streams start in parallel: the kitchen prepares the meals; the waiter prepares the car and then prepares the non-alcoholic beverages; and the sommelier handles alcoholic drink requests. In the alcoholic stream, if wine is desired, the sommelier fetches it from the cellar and then continues. Regardless of the wine choice, the sommelier then checks whether other alcoholic beverages are desired; if so, these alcoholic beverages are prepared, after which the alcoholic stream continues. Once the meals, the non-alcoholic beverages, and the alcoholic drink stream are all ready, the waiter delivers the desired order to the guest (communicated to the guest). After delivery, the waiter waits until there are no other orders to process, then debits the customer’s account, and the customer order is completed.

0.text: The online selling process starts, and the seller displays items on the webpage. The buyer purchases the item, after which the flow reaches a point where purchase orders or reshipment requests converge so the seller proceeds to receive the buyer’s order. The seller then sends the order purchase confirmation and forwards the order to the shipping company, which picks up the item. The shipping company then decides how to proceed: if the outcome is “On Time,” it delivers the item to the customer within the proper dates, after which eBay tracks the order and the process ends with the buyer closing the order. If instead the company does not deliver the purchase, the buyer decides what to do: with the “Money” choice, the buyer asks for a reimbursement, the seller receives this decision and reimburses the money, and the process ends with the purchase not being continued; with the “Item” choice, the buyer asks for a reshipment of the item, which feeds back to the same convergence point so the seller again receives the order and the cycle repeats from there.

0.text: The process starts when a booking request is received by the taxi system from the customer. The customer service operator checks the data in the request and then decides whether the necessary data was provided. If not, a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends. If the data is complete, the operator checks for available cars and then assesses whether any car will be available within the next 30 minutes. If no car is available in that time frame, a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends. If a car is available, the taxi system displays a list of options, after which the operator picks the nearest car together with the client. The system then calculates the time of arrival, the operator books the taxi, and the process concludes by sending a booking confirmation to the customer.

1.text: The process starts when a booking request is received from the customer, after which the customer service operator checks the data provided. If the user has sent the necessary data, the operator checks for available cars and determines whether any are available within the next 30 minutes. If none are available in that timeframe, a cancellation message is sent to the customer and the process ends. 1.text: When the program starts, it opens with an initial step and immediately asks whether to begin a tutorial. If the tutorial is declined, the program proceeds with the standard key assignment and then marks the introduction as completed; if the tutorial is accepted, the tutorial for the controller features is run and then the introduction is likewise completed. From there the flow continues to an announcement selection menu, which leads into a main menu offering several options. Choosing Settings opens the game settings and then returns to the announcement/menu stage. Choosing Load game retrieves the game states and then proceeds; choosing Continue game goes on directly; and choosing Start new game begins a new game. Any of these three (load, continue, or start new) converge on starting the game, after which background music and ambient noise are both launched in parallel; once both are active, the game is reported as loaded, a command prompt is presented, and the process ends as started. At any time from the main menu, selecting To the tutorial opens a step that leads back into the controller-features tutorial, after which the introduction is completed again and control returns to the announcement/menu stage.
