0.text: The process starts when the applicant submits the application (Bewerbung), which triggers receipt at the savings bank. An acknowledgement (Eingangsbestätigung) is sent to the applicant, after which the application is reviewed and its orderliness is checked. If it is in order, the IT department evaluates the application, and based on that assessment the applicant is either rejected or invited. If invited, the applicant is invited, the interview is prepared and then conducted; afterwards it is decided whether the applicant is good. If not, the process proceeds to a rejection path; if yes, the applicant is put on a list, then selected, and approval for hiring is obtained. If hiring is not approved, the process moves to the rejection path; if approved, the applicant is confirmed, a contract is prepared, contract signing takes place, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, and the application process is completed, ending with the applicant being hired. If at the initial check the application is not in order, the process immediately enters the rejection path. That path consolidates all negative outcomes: explicit rejection after assessment, a negative interview result, a decline by the applicant, a hiring decision that is not approved, or a cancellation; in each of these cases a rejection notice (Absage) is sent to the applicant, the application is archived, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

1.text: The process starts when the applicant’s submission arrives from the Applicant pool, triggering the case at the Savings bank. A receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant. The application is then reviewed; if it is in order, the IT department evaluates it and the case proceeds to assess overall suitability. If at this point a rejection decision is reached, the case moves through the internal rejection path and a rejection notice is sent to the applicant; this converges into a follow-up decision point that directs the case to archiving the application documents, after which the process ends with the applicant rejected. If, instead, the evaluation calls for proceeding, an invitation is issued, the interview is prepared and conducted, and the outcome is checked: if the applicant is not good, the case moves to the same rejection path just described; if the applicant is good, the applicant is put on the list, a selection is made, and approval is obtained from the Board of Directors. After approval, the IT department evaluates the application details for contracting, a contract is prepared, contract signing is carried out, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, the application process is completed, and the process ends with the applicant hired. Several exceptional situations are handled: if hiring is not approved, the case is routed to the rejection path; if the applicant declines, the case joins the post-rejection decision point and proceeds to archiving and ends as rejected; and if the case is canceled mid-process, it is sent directly to the archiving step and also ends as rejected. Communications with the applicant occur at three points: the initial application sent in, the receipt confirmation sent back, and, when applicable, the rejection notice.

2.text: The process starts when an application from the applicant arrives. The HR team immediately sends a receipt confirmation to the applicant and then reviews the application, checking whether it is in order. If it is not in order, the case proceeds directly to the rejection path. If it is in order, the IT department evaluates the application, after which a decision is made on the applicant’s suitability: either the applicant is rejected or they are invited. If rejected at this point, the case moves into a consolidation path that leads to sending a rejection to the applicant; this path also collects other outcomes such as a later decline by the applicant or a later decision to reject. The rejection is followed by archiving the application documents, and the process ends with the applicant rejected. If invited, the HR team invites the applicant, prepares the interview, and conducts it. Based on the interview, the applicant is judged again: if not good, the case goes to the same rejection path as above; if good, the applicant is put on the list, then selected, and approval is obtained from the board. After this, the application is evaluated again. If at this stage hiring is not approved or a rejection is decided, the process is routed to the same rejection and archiving path. Otherwise, the applicant is confirmed, a contract is prepared and then signed, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, and the HR team completes the application process, which ends with the applicant hired. Throughout the process, three external communications take place: the applicant initiates the process by submitting the application; the HR team sends a receipt confirmation to the applicant after it arrives; and, if the decision is negative, a rejection notice is sent to the applicant.

3.text: The process starts when an application arrives from the applicant, triggering the receipt of the application and a receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant. The application is then reviewed and a decision is made on whether it is in order. If it is not in order, the case is routed to the rejection path. If it is in order, the IT department evaluates the application and decides on the applicant’s suitability. If the decision is to invite, the applicant is invited, the interview is prepared and then conducted, after which a decision is made on whether the applicant is good. If not, the case is routed to the rejection path. If yes, the applicant is placed on a list, an applicant is selected, and approval is obtained; if approval is not granted, the case is routed to the rejection path. If approval is granted, a contract is prepared and the contract is signed; the applicant is then placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, and the application process is completed, ending with the applicant being hired. The rejection path consistently routes through a series of decisions to send a rejection to the applicant, then proceeds to wrap up and archive the application documents, ending with the applicant being rejected. At any time, if the applicant declines, the case is directed to the wrap-up stage before archiving and rejection; if hiring is not approved during the approval stage, the case is directed to the same rejection routing; and if the process is canceled, it proceeds directly to the wrap-up stage before archiving and rejection.

4.text: The process starts when an application arrives from the applicant, which triggers the handling at the savings bank. A receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant. The application is then reviewed, after which a decision is made on whether the application is in order. If it is not, or if it is later assessed as unsuitable, the case is routed toward rejection. If the application is in order, it is evaluated, and then a decision is made on suitability: if the applicant is to be invited, an invitation is issued, the interview is prepared and conducted, and a decision is taken on whether the applicant is good. A negative decision here routes the case back toward rejection. A positive decision results in putting the applicant on the list and selecting the applicant, after which approval is obtained from the board. If “Hiring was not approved,” the case is redirected toward rejection. If approval is granted, the applicant is confirmed, a contract is prepared, and contract signing is carried out. The applicant is then placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, and the application process is completed, after which the process ends with the applicant hired. If at any time a rejection path is taken, a rejection is issued and sent to the applicant; this and the events “Applicant Declines” or a cancellation lead to the closure stream where the application documents are archived and the process ends with the applicant rejected.

5.text: The process starts when the Applicant sends the “Bewerbung,” which triggers “Application arrives.” The HR team immediately sends a “Eingangsbestätigung” receipt confirmation to the Applicant and then reviews the application to decide “Is the application in order?” If not, the case is routed toward rejection. If it is in order, the IT department evaluates the application, after which a decision is made (“Applicant Suitable?”): if “reject,” the case moves toward rejection; if “invite,” the Applicant is invited, the interview is prepared and conducted, and then “Is the applicant good?” is assessed. A “no” outcome here also routes to rejection, while a “yes” leads to placing the Applicant on the list, selecting the Applicant, obtaining approval from the Board of Directors, confirming the Applicant, preparing the contract, completing “Contract Signing,” placing the Applicant in the position, occupying the position in the system, and completing the application process, after which the process ends with “Applicant Hired.” Any of the following situations send the case to the same rejection handling: a “reject” decision at suitability, a “no” after the interview, an initial application not in order, “Hiring was not approved,” “Applicant Declines,” or a process cancellation. In the rejection handling, HR sends an “Absage” rejection notice to the Applicant, the case proceeds to archive the application documents, and the process ends with “Applicant Rejected.”

6.text: The process starts when the applicant submits an application, which triggers its receipt at the savings bank. A receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant, after which the application is reviewed. A first decision checks whether the application is in order: if not, the case is routed to rejection handling; if yes, the IT department evaluates the application and a suitability decision is made. If the applicant is to be invited, an invitation is issued, the interview is prepared and conducted, and a further decision evaluates the interview result. If the interview result is negative, the case moves to rejection handling; if positive, the applicant is put on a list, then selected, and hiring approval is obtained by the board. If hiring is not approved, the case moves to rejection handling; if approved, the applicant is confirmed, the contract is prepared and signed, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, the application process is completed, and the process ends with the applicant hired. If at any point a rejection is decided (for example because the application was not in order, the applicant was deemed unsuitable, or the interview result was negative), a rejection notice is sent to the applicant and the case advances to closure. If the applicant declines during contract signing, or if the process is canceled, the case also advances to this closure. In all these closure situations, the file is archived and the process ends with the applicant rejected. Communications during the process include the applicant sending the application to start the process, the organization sending the receipt confirmation after intake, and, when applicable, sending the rejection notice to the applicant.

7.text: The process at the savings bank starts when an application is received from the applicant, triggering “Application arrives.” A receipt confirmation is sent to the applicant, after which the application is reviewed and its orderliness is assessed at “Is the application in order?” If yes, the IT department evaluates the application and decides at “Applicant Suitable?” either to invite the applicant (invite) or to reject (reject). If invited, the applicant is invited, the interview is prepared and conducted, and then “Is the applicant good?” is decided: if no, the flow returns to the rejection route; if yes, the applicant is put on the list, the applicant is selected, approval is obtained, and the applicant is confirmed. The contract is then prepared, signing takes place, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, and the application process is completed, which ends with “Applicant Hired.” If instead at “Applicant Suitable?” the outcome is reject, or if the application was not in order, these paths merge and proceed through a routing to a decision that leads to sending a rejection; after the rejection is sent, the process passes through a routing step to a consolidation where three cases are handled: the rejection just issued, a cancellation (caught by a cancellation event), or an applicant decline (caught by an error event). From there, archiving of the application documents follows, and the process ends with “Applicant Rejected.” Additionally, if during approval the outcome “Hiring was not approved” occurs, the process is routed directly to the same decision that leads to sending a rejection. Throughout, two communications with the applicant take place: initially the receipt confirmation is sent, and in the rejection path a rejection notice is sent.

8.text: The process starts when an application is received from the applicant, which triggers the work at the savings bank. First, a receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant. The application is then reviewed, after which it is checked whether the application is in order. If it is, the IT department evaluates the application and decides how to proceed: if the outcome is to invite, the applicant is invited, the interview is prepared and conducted, and it is then assessed whether the applicant is good. If not, the case moves into a rejection path; if yes, the applicant is put on a list and then selected. The selection is submitted for approval; if hiring is not approved, the process is routed to the rejection path. If approval is granted, the applicant is confirmed, the contract is prepared and signed, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is occupied in the system, the application process is completed, and the case ends with the applicant hired. If, at any earlier decision, the application is not in order, if the applicant is assessed as unsuitable, or if the decision at evaluation is to reject, the case proceeds to rejection: a rejection is sent to the applicant, after which the case is routed to finalization where the application documents are archived and the process ends with the applicant rejected. Additionally, if the applicant declines at any point, the process is routed to finalization and archiving as above; likewise, if the process is canceled, it is directed to finalization and archiving. Communications that occur are the incoming application from the applicant that starts the process, the outgoing receipt confirmation sent immediately after receipt, and, in the rejection path, the outgoing rejection notice to the applicant.

9.text: The process at the savings bank begins when the applicant sends in the application, which triggers the receipt of the application and an immediate confirmation is sent back to the applicant. The application is then reviewed, after which a decision is made on whether it is in order: if not, the case moves into the rejection stream; if yes, the IT department evaluates the application and a suitability decision follows. If the outcome is to invite, the applicant is invited, an interview is prepared and conducted, and a further decision is taken on whether the applicant is good: if not, the case goes to the rejection stream; if yes, the applicant is put on the list, a specific candidate is selected, and approval is sought from the board. If hiring is not approved, the case is routed to the same rejection stream; otherwise, the IT department evaluates the application again and the suitability decision is revisited, from which a “reject” outcome also leads to the rejection stream. The rejection stream proceeds through internal decision points to issuing a rejection to the applicant, then a consolidation step, and finally archiving the application documents, after which the process ends with the applicant rejected; this stream can also be entered directly if the applicant declines or if the case is canceled. Separately, once the applicant has been confirmed, the contract is prepared and signed, the applicant is placed in the position, the position is recorded in the system, and the application process is completed, ending with the applicant hired.

Finance checks the customer data and decides how to proceed: if the outcome is to release the order, Finance releases it and communicates this to Service, which then continues processing the order by printing it and forwarding it, ending the process with the customer order forwarded. If the outcome is to reject the order, Finance rejects it and communicates this to Service, which informs the customer, ending the process with the customer informed.

0.text: When a task arises in Viticulture in Outdoor Operations, technical Jane Doe first estimates the working time effort and then determines whether a field employee can be reached. She proceeds to check resource availability, selects a suitable field employee, and contacts them. The employee’s reachability is then checked again: if the employee is reachable (Yes), the task is assigned to the employee, and Jane Doe specifies the procedure for task completion. The field employee receives the task, confirms it, processes the task, and completes it. They then prepare a completion report, after which Jane Doe documents the completion report, and the process ends with the task being processed. If at the reachability check the employee is not reachable (No), the task is marked as not assigned and the process returns to re-evaluate reachability until it can proceed.

0.text: A new marketing campaign is announced at SoKnow, upon which management plans the focal points. Marketing then develops design ideas and defines the specifications, after which an order is sent to the external marketing agency to commission the work. The process waits until the agency’s drafts are received; when they arrive, marketing evaluates the agency drafts and then holds a vote on them. If this vote is positive, marketing informs management, who evaluates the drafts as well. If management’s evaluation is also positive, management gives the green light to marketing, who then conducts the campaign and commissions the agency accordingly; the process concludes when the campaign ends. If the initial vote in marketing is negative, marketing requests new drafts and commissions the agency again; the flow then returns to waiting for new drafts, which, once received, are re-evaluated and re-voted. If management’s evaluation is negative, the process also returns to the point of awaiting further drafts and repeats the reception, evaluation, and voting cycle until a positive decision at both stages is reached.

1.text: When a new marketing campaign is upcoming, management plans the focal points, after which the marketing department designs ideas and defines specifications. The team then sends the order to the external marketing agency, and drafts are later received from the agency. Upon receipt, the process continues by evaluating the agency drafts and then voting on the drafts: if the vote is positive, management is informed; if the vote is negative, the marketing department requests new drafts from the agency and the process returns to the point where newly received drafts are taken up again for evaluation and voting. After management has been informed of a positive vote, management evaluates the drafts and decides whether the evaluation is positive: if not, the process returns to the draft review cycle (back to the point where newly received drafts will again be evaluated and voted on, allowing another request for new drafts if the vote turns out negative); if yes, management gives the green light to the marketing department. With approval granted, the marketing department conducts the campaign, commissions the external agency accordingly, and the process ends when the marketing campaign has concluded.

Likewise, if Management’s evaluation is negative, the process also loops back into that same evaluation track. Throughout the process, communications with the external marketing agency occur three times: when Marketing first commissions the agency after specifications are defined, when Marketing commissions the agency again to request new drafts following a negative vote, and when Marketing commissions the agency to execute the campaign after receiving the green light.

0.text: The process starts when a requirement is recorded, after which offers are obtained and then reviewed. A decision is made based on “Offer > 2000 €?”: if yes, the offer is approved; if no, the offer is not approved. In either case, the flow converges and the goods are ordered. After ordering, a decision is reached about timing: if the delivery is on time, the goods undergo final acceptance; if not, a delivery deadline is set, after which the process loops back into monitoring until timing is acceptable. Once final acceptance is completed, the goods are handed over to goods receipt (communicated externally to the Goods Receipt participant), and the delivery is inspected. A check is made on completeness: if complete, the delivery is confirmed as correct and payment is initiated, which is communicated to Accounting/Controlling; the process then concludes with office supplies purchased. 0.text: The process starts with a planned discharge and proceeds to setting the dismissal date. From there, three activities run in parallel: the medical care needs are determined, the nursing care needs are determined, and the further course is discussed with the patient and relatives. Once all three are completed, the supply facility is defined. This leads to two parallel strands: on one strand, the doctor’s letter is created; on the other, it is decided whether social service is required. If social service is required, further care services are initiated; if not, this is skipped. In both cases, the flow then continues to creating the dismissal documentation. The creation of the doctor’s letter and the dismissal documentation are then synchronized, after which advanced discharge tasks are carried out, and the process concludes with the dismissal.

0.text: The process starts at the customer with Start request, after which the customer sends a request. This request is received by GBI, where it is accepted and processed; alternatively, GBI may independently start the process “Customer Order,” create customer master data, update customer data if needed, and then accept and process the incoming request. GBI then processes the offer and copies the offer to an order, sending the offer to the customer. On the customer side, the offer is received and the customer accepts and processes the customer order, then places the order for bicycles, which is sent to GBI for acceptance and processing of the order. GBI checks inventory; if the product is available, the team requests the product in stock; if it is not available, they procure/order the goods. In both cases, the flow continues with processing the customer order, creating the delivery note, performing inventory control, picking the material, and packing/loading the material to send to the customer; the goods are transmitted to the customer, who performs goods receipt. After shipment, GBI checks inventory, creates the invoice, and sends it to the customer; the customer receives the invoice and settles it, sending the payment back to GBI, which then processes the incoming payment, edits and displays the document flow, and completes its process at The process completed. On the customer side, after goods receipt the customer receives the invoice and settles it, and the customer’s flow ends at Order finished.

1.text: At Customer The Bike Zone, the process starts when a request is initiated and the request is sent to GBI, where, in parallel, the customer order process begins with creating customer master data and, if needed, changing customer data; upon receiving the inquiry, the request is accepted and processed, an offer is prepared, and the offer is copied to an order and sent back to the customer. The customer then accepts and processes the customer order and places a bicycle order to GBI. GBI accepts and processes the order, checks inventory, and decides whether the product is available: if available, the product is requested from stock; if not, it is procured/ordered; in both cases, processing continues with the customer order, a delivery note is created, inventory control is performed, material is picked, and the goods are packed/loaded and sent to the customer. The customer receives the goods and then receives the invoice from GBI, after which the customer settles the invoice and the customer-side process finishes. On GBI’s side, after dispatching the goods, inventory is checked, an invoice is created and sent to the customer, the incoming payment is processed (also confirming receipt of the customer’s payment), the document flow is edited and displayed, and the GBI process completes.

An offer is prepared and processed, then converted into an order and sent to the customer (“Angebot”), after which GBI accepts and processes the order received from the customer. GBI checks the inventory and decides whether the product is available: if it is, a request for product-in-stock is raised; if not, goods are procured/ordered. In both cases, the flow converges to processing the customer order, followed by creating the delivery note, performing inventory control, picking the material, and packing/loading it for shipment to the customer; the goods (“Ware”) are sent and received by the customer in “Goods Receipt.” Upon receipt, the customer proceeds to “Receive invoice,” which arrives from GBI after GBI checks inventory post-shipment, creates the invoice, and sends it to the customer (“Rechnung”); the customer then settles the invoice, and the payment (“Zahlung”) is communicated to GBI, where the incoming payment is processed. 0.text: The process starts and moves to a checkpoint that serves as the entry point for each cycle. The request is then verified, after which the order is sent for request handling, received, and subsequently logged and categorized. The next step determines whether the request is authorized. If it is not authorized, control returns to the initial checkpoint and the cycle begins again with a new verification. If it is authorized, the work splits so that request monitoring and escalation run in parallel with request model execution; both proceed independently and then rejoin. The process continues with request closure and evaluation, followed by a check on whether there was any problem with request processing or the request record. If a problem is identified, the process ends by contacting the incident manager about the problem. If no problem is found, request fulfilment support is performed, and the process concludes successfully.

1.text: The process starts and immediately moves to the first step, where the Incident Manager verifies the request. The Incident Manager then sends the order for request handling to 1st Level Support, who receives the order and performs request logging and categorization. The request is then checked for authorization; if it is not authorized, the flow returns to the first step and the Incident Manager verifies the request again. If it is authorized, work is split so that Request Monitoring and Escalation (handled jointly by the Incident Manager and 1st Level Support) and Request Model Execution (by the Service Request Fulfilment Group with 1st Level Support) run in parallel. Once both are completed, the paths rejoin and 1st Level Support carries out Request Closure and Evaluation. Afterward, it is assessed whether there was a problem with the request processing or the Request Record: if yes, the process ends by contacting the incident manager about the problem; if no, the Incident Manager performs Request Fulfilment Support and the process concludes with a successful end.

0.text: The process starts with an order intake at SoKnow, after which the development department acquires the knowledge management system and awaits the customer’s adjustment requests; once these are received from the customer company, the team makes the requested adjustments and notifies the customer that the changes have been made. The team then searches for a suitable test group and proceeds to conduct tests. The test outcome is awaited: if the result is positive, test group workshops are conducted, followed by employee training. During or after training, the team may receive further adjustment requests from the customer; if such requests arise, the process branches into a refinement cycle where further adjustments are performed and work continues toward finishing the product. If no further requests are raised at that point, the work proceeds toward completing the product and the team signals that the product is finished, notifying the customer accordingly. The customer’s satisfaction with the adjustments is then evaluated: if the adjustments are satisfactory, the system is implemented and the order is completed; if not, the process returns to the refinement cycle where additional adjustments are carried out and the product is steered again toward completion. If, earlier during testing, the result is negative, the team makes additional adjustments and returns to the testing step to await the outcome again, repeating this loop until a positive result is achieved. Throughout the process, notifications are sent to the customer when adjustments are completed and when the product is finished, and the customer can send new adjustment requests at two points: before testing begins and after training, which feed into the respective adjustment cycles.

1.text: The process starts with order intake at SoKnow, after which the development department purchases the knowledge management system and then awaits adjustment requests from the customer company; once these are received, the team makes the requested adjustments and notifies the customer that the adjustments have been made. The team then searches for a suitable test group and proceeds to conduct tests. The test results are evaluated: if the outcome is positive, test group workshops are carried out, followed by training of employees; after training, the team waits again for possible customer adjustment requests, and upon receipt decides whether such requests exist (Yes/No). If Yes, the requests are routed to an internal decision point to determine how to handle them, leading to further adjustments and a subsequent internal review; if No, the process moves directly to the internal review. This internal review culminates in the product being declared finished and the customer being notified, after which the question “Adjustments satisfactory?” is evaluated. If the answer is Yes, the knowledge management system is implemented and the order is completed. If the answer is No, the process returns to handle the new adjustments via the internal decision point, the team makes further adjustments, the internal review is performed again, the product is once more declared finished and the customer is notified, and the question about the satisfaction with adjustments is reconsidered; this loop continues until the answer becomes Yes. Alternatively, if during the earlier test evaluation the result is negative, the team makes further adjustments and returns to the earlier decision before testing to repeat testing and evaluation; this loop iterates until a positive test result leads to workshops and training, after which the process follows the same post-training path described above.

2.text: The process starts with order intake at SoKnow and proceeds to purchasing the Knowledge Management System. The team then waits to receive adjustment requests from the customer company; once these arrive, they make the requested adjustments and notify the customer that the adjustments have been made. Next, they search for a suitable test group and decide to run tests. After the tests, they await test results: if the outcome is negative, they make further adjustments and return to the test setup to run another test cycle; if the outcome is positive, they conduct workshops with the test group and then train employees. After training, they wait to receive any additional adjustment requests from the customer; upon receipt, they assess whether these requests are to be applied (“Yes”) or not (“No”). If “Yes,” they continue to an internal review of whether the overall adjustments are satisfactory; if “No,” they proceed directly to review the product as finished. In both cases, the path converges in a product-finished review that triggers a notification to the customer. Based on this review, if the adjustments are satisfactory (“Yes”), the system is implemented and the order is completed; if they are not satisfactory (“No”), further adjustments are made and the product is reviewed again, with the result sent to the customer, repeating this cycle until the adjustments are deemed satisfactory and the system can be implemented to complete the order.
